title: The Shema
lead: The Shema ("Listen!") is Deuteronomy 6:4–9, Israel's great confession that the LORD is one and the command to love him with all one's heart, being and strength. Jews say it morning and evening with 11:13–21 and Numbers 15:37–41, and Jesus called it the first commandment of all (Mark 12:29–30).

sections.h: The Shema through the Bible and after
sections.b: The Shema's words (Deuteronomy 6:4–9) echo through later Scripture. Joshua 22:5 and 2 Kings 23:25 praise loving God with all the heart and being; Josiah is the one king said to have turned to the LORD "with all his heart, with all his being and with all his strength" (a translation made for this note), in the Shema's own terms. Zechariah 14:9 looks to a day when the LORD will be one and his name one. Jesus calls the Shema the first command (Mark 12:29–30), and Paul restates it in 1 Corinthians 8:6. The Mishnah opens with the rules for reciting it morning and evening (Mishnah Berakhot 1:1–3), and it remains the center of Jewish prayer.
